meta.title: Border closures: global atlas
meta.geometry_source_note: Natural Earth reference boundaries and separately sourced crossing references. Present-day geometry is not historical closure evidence. Duration scope may be narrower than the record reference geography.

rationale_definitions.Interstate disputes and pressure: Political confrontation, retaliation, sanctions or pressure between states or territorial authorities across a frontier. Includes regional sanctions and disputes over territorial status or border administration. De facto authorities are identified without deciding sovereignty. Exclusions: Do not add merely because a closure crosses a border, follows fighting, or involves a foreign actor. A political dispute or pressure mechanism must be documented.
rationale_definitions.Power and regime politics: Seizure, retention or contestation of governing power, regime legitimacy or control of public institutions. Includes coups, succession, political opposition, democratic reform and conflict between rival governing or party authorities, including transnational party conflicts. Exclusions: Routine policy or livelihood demands alone do not establish regime contestation. External sanctions seeking a regime change belong under Interstate disputes and pressure unless a separate domestic mechanism is also evidenced.
rationale_definitions.Policy and socioeconomic demands: Documented demands to change public policy, employment, services or economic conditions, where the obstruction is intended to press those demands. Code the demand, not merely the fact that a protest occurred. Exclusions: Do not infer specific demands from an unspecified protest or use this label for every strike. Regime change or institutional power contests belong under Power and regime politics.
rationale_definitions.Health and biosecurity: Health and biosecurity replaces Public health. Human disease control and animal/plant disease control remain distinct. Health-policy opposition belongs under Policy and socioeconomic demands.
rationale_definitions.Security / Armed conflict and military c: Hostilities, armed-group control, military standoffs or threatened military action. Does not settle responsibility or establish a hidden military objective.
rationale_definitions.Security / Armed attacks and terrorism: A reported attack, assassination or threat of armed attack. Terrorism allegations remain attributed; inclusion does not itself designate an actor as terrorist.
rationale_definitions.Security / Crime and law enforcement: Crime prevention, criminal investigations, kidnappings or law-enforcement concerns beyond the separately coded smuggling purpose.
rationale_definitions.Security / Smuggling and illicit traffic: Preventing or responding to alleged illicit movement of goods, currency, weapons or people. Allegations are not treated as established criminal findings.
rationale_definitions.Security / Public order and immediate sa: Protection of travellers, staff or property; crowd control, unrest, safe port operation or event security.
rationale_definitions.Security / Espionage and hostile interfe: Attributed intelligence threats, espionage or deliberate cross-border interference. Allegations, including instrumentalised migration, remain attributed rather than established.
rationale_definitions.Security / Unspecified security: Security is supported at the broad level, but a more specific purpose is not established.
rationale_definitions.Health and biosecurity / Human disease c: Preventing introduction or transmission of human disease, including screening, quarantine and disinfection. Opposition to health rules is coded under policy demands.
rationale_definitions.Health and biosecurity / Animal and plan: Veterinary, phytosanitary and other animal/plant biosecurity objectives. Does not imply a human-health threat or a protectionist intention.
rationale_definitions.Trade and protectionism / Import, export: Restrictions on goods or market access, including economic protection and documented export controls. An instrument can establish the restriction without establishing all underlying motives.
rationale_definitions.Trade and protectionism / Customs and tr: Customs, tariffs, routing, vehicle eligibility or cargo-transfer rules that are themselves the documented rationale or policy content.
rationale_definitions.Trade and protectionism / Currency contr: Restrictions associated with banknote withdrawal, currency circulation or financial controls.
rationale_definitions.Trade and protectionism / Trade and tran: Commercial actors obstructing passage to seek changes in trade rules, market access, transport charges or customs services. Does not imply a government protectionist closure.
rationale_definitions.Trade and protectionism / Unspecified tr: A commercial or trade-policy rationale is recorded, but the evidence does not support a narrower subtype.
rationale_definitions.Migration / Entry and asylum control: Regulating or preventing migration admission, including nationality and asylum procedures. A travel restriction solely for health or security is not automatically a migration rationale.
rationale_definitions.Migration / Exit control: A documented migration purpose concerning departure. Direction alone does not establish this rationale.
rationale_definitions.Migration / Transit control: A documented migration purpose concerning onward passage. Direction alone does not establish this rationale.
rationale_definitions.Migration / Processing capacity: Suspension to reassign personnel or facilities to processing migrant arrivals.
rationale_definitions.Migration / Admission and document dispu: Disputes or protests over admission, repatriation, transit permission or travel documents. This includes demands to allow passage, not only efforts to prevent it.
rationale_definitions.Migration / Unspecified migration ration: Migration is recorded as relevant, but purpose or direction remains insufficiently resolved.
rationale_definitions.Electoral politics / Election administra: Conduct, integrity, staffing or security of voting. Add Security only where a security/public-order justification is separately recorded.
rationale_definitions.Electoral politics / Electoral disputes: Restrictions or obstruction connected to an explicitly documented dispute over an election, its result or a transition timetable.
rationale_definitions.Electoral politics / Voter access and pa: Obstruction intended to affect travel by voters or participation in an election.
rationale_definitions.Interstate disputes and pressure / Sanct: Border restrictions used to obtain concessions or change another authority's conduct, including formal regional sanctions. Includes clearly attributed reporting interpretations.
rationale_definitions.Interstate disputes and pressure / Diplo: Restrictions connected to a documented dispute, retaliatory measure or rupture of relations between authorities.
rationale_definitions.Interstate disputes and pressure / Terri: Disputes over boundaries, cross-border works, territory or sovereign status. Coding does not determine sovereignty or recognise de facto authorities as states.
rationale_definitions.Interstate disputes and pressure / Unspe: An interstate or inter-authority dispute is recorded without sufficient detail for a narrower subtype.
rationale_definitions.Power and regime politics / Coups and su: Seizure, transfer or consolidation of governing power, including a documented coup or succession context. Does not infer a distinct closure motive absent evidence.
rationale_definitions.Power and regime politics / Opposition a: Contestation of leadership, regime legitimacy, political participation or constitutional reform.
rationale_definitions.Power and regime politics / Contested go: Rival institutions, parties or armed authorities contesting jurisdiction or control of a crossing.
rationale_definitions.Power and regime politics / Unspecified: A power or regime dispute is recorded, but a narrower purpose is not established.
rationale_definitions.Policy and socioeconomic demands / Oppos: Demands to remove or change pandemic restrictions, testing rules or health-policy charges. Does not imply infection prevention as the protest's purpose.
rationale_definitions.Policy and socioeconomic demands / Jobs,: Employment, wages, working conditions, public services, infrastructure or household economic demands.
rationale_definitions.Policy and socioeconomic demands / Right: Documented grievances concerning rights, policing, land, environmental projects or a specified policy dispute outside the other subtypes.
rationale_definitions.Policy and socioeconomic demands / Unspe: A policy or socioeconomic purpose is established but cannot be narrowed. Do not use merely because unspecified protesters oppose a government.
rationale_definitions.Taxonomy A_authorisation — Administratio: An attributed administrative purpose concerning the legally authorised checkpoint roster or consolidation of crossing services. Do not infer a security or political purpose from an administrative act alone.
rationale_definitions.Taxonomy A_service — Administration and: A deliberate temporary suspension for a documented administrative occasion or service arrangement, such as a facility inauguration. Accidental breakdowns and routine overnight opening hours do not become eligible closures merely by receiving this code.
rationale_definitions.Taxonomy ENV_conservation — Environment: A documented purpose of protecting a nature reserve, habitat or wildlife. Distinct from animal or plant disease control and from an unsupported inference based on geography.
rationale_definitions.Taxonomy ENV_husbandry — Environment and: A documented purpose of controlling cross-border livestock herds, grazing rights or responsibility for straying animals. Disease prevention requires its own evidence and code.
rationale_definitions.Health and biosecurity / Food safety and: Preventing human exposure to unsafe or contaminated food, including aflatoxin or mycotoxin contamination, when explicitly attributed to the restricting authority or reported as its stated reason. Do not infer disease transmission, animal or plant pathogens, or protectionist intent from a food-safety restriction.

timing_coverage.Dimension: Counts are parent records, not phases. Evidence categories can overlap. Rationale categories are nonexclusive. Complete operational excludes censored, same-day, policy, ordered, intermittent and expressly contested periods. Exact complete is a stricter subset. Missing evidence is nonrandom; these figures do not support population duration averages or closed-day totals.

limitations: Incomplete, nonrandom inventory; evidence coverage is not closure incidence.
Records, phases and rationale groups may overlap and must not be summed as independent closures.
Held or contested phases are shown only at recorded evidence dates, not as confirmed intervals.
Last observations, schedules and legal transitions do not establish reopening; the later state remains unknown.
Same-model AI review does not establish human or different-model validation.

release_method.full_text: The dataset was compiled using OpenAI’s GPT‑6 Astra with Ultra reasoning, with GPT‑6 Astra Pro documented in the final research and review logs. The work comprised 16 initial research rounds, including three full-register verification exercises, followed by two further register-wide reviews and 50 additional research and review cycles. Six regional AI reviewers contributed to major assessments, with research, challenge and adjudication conducted in separate contexts of the same model. Reviewers checked whether each restriction occurred, its start and endpoint, the crossings and types of movement affected, continuity, and the reported reasons against linked source evidence. The two subsequent register-wide exercises comprised a blind reconstruction and challenge of 653 records, producing 3,918 claim assessments, and a further assessment of all 686 records and 738 phases in the expanded register. Additional chronology work assessed 519 cases and subjected 272 unresolved cases to fresh research and separate review. The final 50 cycles comprised 30 coverage-search cycles, ten targeted-verification cycles and ten audits of preselected records, providing full-record source reviews of 160 entries and addressing 176 targeted questions across 162 entries. Proposed additions were checked against existing episodes to avoid duplication, while partial reopenings and changes in restrictions were recorded as separate phases. The resulting register contains 829 records and 1,010 phases, supported by a catalogue of 4,680 distinct recorded URLs. Automated consistency checks covered the complete final dataset; uncertain dates, source-access limitations and unresolved claims remain explicit. The five register-wide reviews covered successive versions of the dataset, while the later targeted audits examined selected records.

historical_research_method.verification_statement: Six regional AI reviewers and root integration; same model contexts, not independent human or different-model verification. Source access and unresolved attributes remain explicit.
historical_research_method.review_limits: Source access and unresolved attributes remain explicit. Initial findings are retained as historical review, with subsequent findings in Follow-up review. Coverage is reported by original region and each nonexclusive rationale. A record coded to several rationales appears in each applicable row. Counts measure evidence coverage, not the incidence of closures or causal effects. Exact complete operational periods form a stricter sensitivity subset of all complete operational periods. No pooled average, regional ranking or aggregate closed-day total is inferred from this incomplete, nonrandom set.
historical_research_method.current_vs_historical: Current Register, Chronology phases, Follow-up review and correction-release Codebook rules supersede initial findings and explicitly labelled historical snapshots.

duration_review.precision_rule: Chronology phases records observed reopening as Yes, No or Unknown. Scheduled expiry, legal transition and last observation are not observed reopening. Partial resumption applies only to the named traffic and direction.
duration_review.counting_rule: Minimum and maximum values are date-boundary differences. Endpoint inclusion is recorded separately and does not trigger an automatic +1 day. Reported order lengths and clock times remain source-specific.
duration_review.mapping_rule: Every phase has an explicit location decision. Use only approved_approximate links with that phase temporal display rule. Reject wrong-crossing matches. Unlocated coordinates stay blank. Controlled traffic/direction tags are partial; original phase text and exceptions remain authoritative. Sixteen approved phase links use nine approximate published markers, not surveyed gates.
duration_review.coverage_rule: Coverage is reported by original region and each nonexclusive rationale. A record coded to several rationales appears in each applicable row. Counts measure evidence coverage, not the incidence of closures or causal effects. Exact complete operational periods form a stricter sensitivity subset of all complete operational periods. No pooled average, regional ranking or aggregate closed-day total is inferred from this incomplete, nonrandom set.
duration_review.rationale_rule: Assignments are nonexclusive and attributed. A documented reason is not proof of complete or true motive. Five supported administrative/environmental reasons receive four new subtypes; other assignments are not automatically recoded. Uncoded known reasons remain distinct from unknown reasons.
duration_review.verification_rule: Six regional AI reviewers and root integration; same model contexts, not independent human or different-model verification. Source access and unresolved attributes remain explicit.
duration_review.continuity_rule: Confirmed evidence stops at its dated limit. The following state is unknown unless the same scoped phase has an observed reopening. Unmarked geography never establishes openness.
duration_review.held_rule: A contested phase supplies held date markers at its recorded boundaries or observations, not a confirmed interval. The Atlas labels these markers and warns when a searched record has no evidence in the selected month. Two included records lack dated phases and remain searchable in All dates.
duration_review.scope_rule: Land-border register retained. Island-state air admission restrictions remain outside this release pending the separate airport integration. Short land closures are retained.

historical_codebook.Scope: International land borders worldwide, including separately identified disputed/de facto settings; active at any point from 21 October 2016 to 21 October 2026. Earlier closures may appear if active within the window.
historical_codebook.Earlier stage — pre-correction: Round 16: 31 candidate leads assessed; 15 additions; 20 still held. 1 quarantined. No global near-completeness claim.
historical_codebook.Main fields: Register records chronology, rationale and uncertainty. Dimensions retains the six axes in the supplied draft. Evidence links each record to source provenance; Claim checks identifies support for particular fields.
historical_codebook.Well-supported: The defined central occurrence/order and its limited scope have sufficient evidence. This is not a claim that every field or all enforcement is settled. Read endpoint and uncertainty columns.
historical_codebook.Partially-supported: Occurrence/order has evidence, but material onset, endpoint, scope or source-access questions remain.
historical_codebook.Provisional: Retained for visibility and follow-up. Weak access, contradictory reporting or incomplete corroboration prevents firm analytical use.
historical_codebook.Lead: Potential episode, unscreened search target or explicitly excluded claim. Not counted as a closure record.
historical_codebook.Source count: Reporting origins are descriptive. Shared official announcements or wire syndication may be one evidence chain. Evidence quality and claim specificity determine assessment, not a fixed source count.
historical_codebook.Dates: Exact dates are native spreadsheet dates. YYYY-MM and YYYY are text at the precision justified by evidence. Blank means not established, not zero.
historical_codebook.Announcement versus operation: Announced reopening is scheduled or ordered. Formal permission or repeal records an enacted legal change without establishing operational resumption. Actual or partial reopening refers only to the stated scope.
historical_codebook.Calendar days: Calculated only for exact dates and an observed reopening endpoint. Endpoint minus onset gives calendar-date difference, not exact hours or necessarily continuous prohibition for every category.
historical_codebook.Imprecise intervals: Where both endpoints are known only by month/year, Duration qualification may give a range derived from the first/last possible dates. These are bounds to the stated endpoint, not a full-closure estimate.
historical_codebook.Subday: Same-day interruptions are described in text. A date difference of zero must not be interpreted as no closure.
historical_codebook.Open-ended: No duration is extended to 21 October 2026 merely because reopening was not found. Use the last confirmed closed observation, where available.
historical_codebook.Rationale codes: Security; Health and biosecurity; Trade and protectionism; Migration; Electoral politics; Interstate disputes and pressure; Power and regime politics; Policy and socioeconomic demands. Broad categories and subcategories are non-exclusive. Register column P shows the hierarchy; Rationale coding provides one row per assignment with its evidence basis and phase.
historical_codebook.Direction and groups: Different states, directions, nationalities, passengers, freight and humanitarian movements may operate under different rules at the same crossing.
historical_codebook.Enforcement: A decree establishes formal policy. Actual permeability and informal passage require operational or field evidence. An unspecified field is not a finding of no exceptions or effects.
historical_codebook.Related records: Regional sanctions, national implementation and individual-crossing phases can overlap. Deduplicate by authority, geography, population, time and policy before statistical analysis.
historical_codebook.Coercive closures: Intentional military action that prevents movement through an official crossing can be a de facto closure. Natural disasters and accidental infrastructure outages are ancillary. This does not establish a motive for the attack.
historical_codebook.COVID screen: External COBAP rows selected by LAND=1 or COMPLETE policy type. These are discovery candidates, not independently verified additions; many complete policies concern island air/sea entry. Raw external dates use MM_DD_YY. Check original source, geography, exceptions, sequence and duplicate coverage.
historical_codebook.Source access: Full page means the page content was retrieved. Search extract means only indexed text was available and is weaker evidence. Published sources are not automatically independent observations.
historical_codebook.Coverage exclusions: Routine nightly hours, individual visa denials, screening without a prohibition, and airport/sea-only closures are outside the core inventory. Disputed territories and external boundaries are identified in the dimensions.
historical_codebook.Land scope: Air- and sea-only restrictions remain outside scope. River ferries across an international frontier are included. Some islands, such as Hispaniola and New Guinea, have land frontiers.
historical_codebook.Research basis: Full audit and Source review preserve round5 history. Rounds7–14 were bounded checks. Round15 examines all629 baseline rows; its audit tab records fresh claim assessments and access limits, not a claim that every fact is confirmed.
historical_codebook.Extension: Six claim checks govern evidence. Unknown facts remain null. Read current quarantine and inclusion notes; evidence lineages are not independent merely because publishers differ.
historical_codebook.Reproducibility: Current conclusions are in Register, Durations and Chronology phases. Original parent claims and numbered-round sheets remain historical. Follow-up review records the correction pass and unresolved questions; no review completion is a blanket verification.

Exclusions: Do not add merely because a closure crosses a border, follows fighting, or involves a foreign actor. A political dispute or pressure mechanism must be documented.

historical_codebook.Rationale revision scope: All 653 current records were reviewed, including the quarantined record. Its exclusion is preserved. This revision changes rationale coding only, retaining chronology, sources, scope, factual assessments outside rationale and historical records.
historical_codebook.Evidence basis: Attributed official justification records a stated explanation, not proof of its truth or completeness. Reported reason is attributed through the source record. Analytical interpretation of reported context is explicitly separate. Unresolved attribution retains an inherited broad component without upgrading its evidence.
historical_codebook.Unassigned replacements: A known reason outside the taxonomy is distinguished from an unknown reason. Neither is replaced with a guessed category.
historical_codebook.Verification status: This is a taxonomy and coding review, not an additional research cycle or evidence that every record received triple verification.
historical_codebook.Multiple rationales: Categories and subcategories are non-exclusive. Retain every independently supported rationale; never require a single primary rationale. Do not infer an additional purpose merely from affected goods, migrants, a government actor or the existence of a protest.
historical_codebook.Phases and concurrent aims: Multiple codes can describe concurrent purposes, different actors or successive phases. Use the phase and evidence notes; do not assume all reasons applied throughout the entire record.
historical_codebook.Counting rationale categories: Exclude quarantined records and count distinct record IDs within each category. Do not sum subcategory rows into a parent total. Categories overlap, so percentages can sum to more than 100%. Related records can also overlap in policy, geography and time; rationale counts are not counts of independent closure events.

historical_codebook.Historical snapshot — Duration review: f: 22 October 2026: 653 rows screened; 116 included records have reviewed playback periods (46 carried forward, 37 restored, 8 targeted chronology decisions, 25 same-day episodes). 536 await chronology review; GL18 remains excluded. Register S–T links to the Durations sheet.
historical_codebook.precision rule: Use exact calendar dates when supported, otherwise explicit earliest/latest bounds. No default ±3-day allowance or invented midpoint.
historical_codebook.scope rule: A start and endpoint must concern the same movement, direction and phase. Exemptions remain explicit. A partial reopening ends only its stated scope.
historical_codebook.counting rule: Calendar days are end date minus start date, not measured elapsed hours. Same-day episodes have no numeric whole-day duration. Related phases are not independent campaigns.
historical_codebook.mapping rule: Month overlap uses [start date, endpoint date); same-day episodes are shown only in their event month. Confirmed-through periods include their last evidence date. Bounded dates can yield possible-only overlap, shown distinctly. No unknown endpoint is extended to the research cutoff.
historical_codebook.Historical snapshot — verification rule: This is an additive chronology review, not a fourth register-wide verification or a new triple verification. Forty-six prior atlas intervals are carried forward; archived evidence was reconciled for restored and same-day records, and selected cases received targeted retrieval. Fresh source checks may reproduce the same underlying reporting origin.
historical_codebook.coverage rule: A missing marker means no eligible period is displayed, not that a border was open. Timing remains unresolved for pending records, which stay visible in All dates and in the review queue.
historical_codebook.preservation rule: Original dates, interval_days, continuity flags, claim checks, rationales and sources are preserved. New scoped decisions supersede the old strict animation exclusion only for this additive layer.
historical_codebook.Historical snapshot — Duration evidence: Twelve targeted retrieval checks for eight records are documented in duration_review_20261022/Duration_source_checks.csv. Other new decisions use archived evidence. This tranche is not a new triple verification; no human or independent-model review is implied.
historical_codebook.Historical snapshot — Legacy GIS interva: The web atlas uses the new duration periods. QGIS interval layers retain the 46 strict legacy intervals; the complete GIS event layers carry new duration bounds as attributes.
historical_codebook.Historical snapshot — Duration review: s: 22 October 2026: 20 records reviewed; 17 periods admitted (11 scoped restrictions and 6 formal policy periods), 3 held. Current web playback covers 133 records; 519 remain pending. The original 116 periods are unchanged.
historical_codebook.Formal policy periods: Formal policy periods measure the time a specified prohibition remained in force. They are labelled separately and do not establish first actual refusal, passage or complete physical enforcement. A selected legal phase is not the original onset of a broader campaign.
historical_codebook.Historical snapshot — Second-tranche evi: Thirty-seven access checks distinguish full, indexed and failed retrievals and shared reporting origins. Chi Ma March–April 2022, Vicovu January 2024 and Ghana COVID remain pending after review. See duration_review_batch2_20261022/Duration_batch2_source_checks.csv and duration_batch2.json.
historical_codebook.Historical snapshot — Duration review as: The second tranche used source retrieval, scope/continuity reconciliation and date/formula checks. It is not a new triple verification or independent human/model review. Historical triple-verification statements are not extended to these new duration decisions.
historical_codebook.Historical snapshot — Earlier full durat: All 519 previously pending records individually assessed: 247 new scoped periods; 272 reviewed but unresolved; 0 unreviewed. With the 133 unchanged earlier periods, 380 of 652 included records support playback. GL18 remains quarantined. Assessment completion does not mean every duration is known.
historical_codebook.Date bounds and selected segments: Calendar-day boundaries use source-supported dates or explicit earliest/latest bounds. Month/year-level onsets remain broad. No blanket +/-3-day tolerance or exact elapsed-hour claim is applied. Zero minimum under overlapping bounds is not a zero-duration finding; same-day periods have no numeric day measurement. A selected segment may end at a partial opening or exclude earlier/later phases.
historical_codebook.Policy and confirmed-through periods: Formal policy periods and formal-policy confirmed-through segments are labelled separately. They describe the documented rule or selected phase, not uniform physical enforcement, first actual refusal or first traffic resumption. Missing renewal chains are retained as qualifications or grounds for withholding a period. Confirmed-through rows use column J as last evidence, with no reopening date in H/I and no maximum duration in L.
historical_codebook.Historical snapshot — Review and evidenc: This is one-agent, record-by-record reconciliation of archived evidence notes, source lineages and contrary claim checks, with 15 targeted fresh source-access entries. Retrieval status distinguishes full, indexed and failed access; syndicated reports are not independent confirmations. Separate scope/continuity and date/formula tests reduce specific errors but do not make the review independent. No new triple verification, independent-model review or human validation is claimed. Earlier register-wide verification claims are not extended to these new duration decisions. See duration_full_decisions.json and Duration_full_source_checks.csv.
historical_codebook.Historical snapshot — Unresolved records: The 272-row Duration_followup_queue.csv gives an individual reason or next evidence need for every unresolved case. They remain in All dates, not duration playback. Map geometry is unchanged record-level context. A narrower duration does not apply automatically to every linked crossing or the entire displayed frontier.
historical_codebook.Historical snapshot — Earlier chronology: 272/272 fresh research decisions and 272/272 separate new-decision reviews; 37/37 deliberate baseline challenges. 573 records have any dated evidence; 257 have a complete scoped operational period. 79 have no admitted dated phase.
historical_codebook.Evidence categories: Formal policy periods describe legal or documented rule lifetimes, ordered windows describe schedules whose actual enforcement is unverified, and intermittent-regime envelopes do not measure days continuously closed. These categories must not be pooled as operational closure durations.
historical_codebook.Phases and duration arithmetic: End date minus start date measures calendar-day boundary differences, not elapsed hours. Bounded periods retain minimum/maximum uncertainty, except correlated endpoint alternatives where independent subtraction would be invalid and the numeric result is withheld. Same-day episodes and intermittent regimes have no numeric closed-day measure. Confirmed-through evidence is right-censored with no maximum or inferred reopening. Multiple phases can overlap by movement or scope and must not be summed automatically.
historical_codebook.Historical snapshot — Review limits and: All 272 previously unresolved records received targeted fresh searches and individual decisions, followed by a separate same-model AI review. A deliberate 37-record baseline challenge covered the 12 longest periods plus deterministic regional selections; this is not a representative audit sample. Actual source access is logged as full, indexed excerpt or failed. Shared reporting origins are retained. No human validation, different-model independence, exhaustive source retrieval or new triple verification is claimed.
historical_codebook.Coverage and missingness: Coverage is reported by original region and each nonexclusive rationale. A record coded to several rationales appears in each applicable row. Counts measure evidence coverage, not the incidence of closures or causal effects. Exact complete operational periods form a stricter sensitivity subset of all complete operational periods. No pooled average, regional ranking or aggregate closed-day total is inferred from this incomplete, nonrandom set.
historical_codebook.Earlier snapshot — Current spreadsheet r: 44 existing records reviewed, 22 amended, 12 new records admitted. Research stages completed does not mean all evidence questions were resolved. The 2016-10-21 to 2026-10-21 window remains fixed.
historical_codebook.Earlier snapshot — Current review proven: The 23 October pass used a primary AI reviewer only, without a separate challenge. Earlier blind reconstructions and separate same-model checks remain historical and are retained in the preceding audit. None of these are human or different-model validation. Full, indexed and failed access remain distinct.
historical_codebook.Calculation ownership: Rationale coding owns assignments. Register joins unique broad labels by record ID using TEXTJOIN, UNIQUE and FILTER; Durations reads that single joined result. These require modern Excel or another compatible calculator. Chronology phases owns scoped dates and arithmetic. Record-ID joins withstand sorting. Multiple phases remain separate. Timing coverage counts only Included parents.
historical_codebook.Earlier snapshot — Current versus histor: Register D:R contains current status or explicitly labelled historical parent evidence. Original dates/calculations stay in S:W. Historical parent-claim checks do not automatically verify later narrower phases. Earlier Codebook snapshots and Timing coverage O:P remain historical.
historical_codebook.Date and endpoint rules: Only source-supported dates or explicit bounds. Same-day and intermittent regimes have no whole-day duration. A last-confirmed date is not a reopening, and an endpoint upper bound is not an exact event date. Ordered and formal policy periods do not establish operational gate continuity. Calendar endpoint differences are not exact elapsed hours.
historical_codebook.Rationale and phase rules: Assignments are nonexclusive and attributed. A documented reason is not proof of complete or true motive. Five supported administrative/environmental reasons receive four new subtypes; other assignments are not automatically recoded. Uncoded known reasons remain distinct from unknown reasons.
historical_codebook.Queue and coverage: Unresolved queue states the next evidence needed. Search coverage records actual queries, candidates and negative results; country-year coverage is only documented partial effort. No results from a query does not establish that no closure occurred.
historical_codebook.Phase geometry and traffic rules: Every phase has an explicit location decision. Use only approved_approximate links with that phase temporal display rule. Reject wrong-crossing matches. Unlocated coordinates stay blank. Controlled traffic/direction tags are partial; original phase text and exceptions remain authoritative. Sixteen approved phase links use nine approximate published markers, not surveyed gates.
historical_codebook.Taxonomy A_authorisation — Administratio: An attributed administrative purpose concerning the legally authorised checkpoint roster or consolidation of crossing services. Do not infer a security or political purpose from an administrative act alone.
historical_codebook.Taxonomy A_service — Administration and: A deliberate temporary suspension for a documented administrative occasion or service arrangement, such as a facility inauguration. Accidental breakdowns and routine overnight opening hours do not become eligible closures merely by receiving this code.
historical_codebook.Taxonomy ENV_conservation — Environment: A documented purpose of protecting a nature reserve, habitat or wildlife. Distinct from animal or plant disease control and from an unsupported inference based on geography.
historical_codebook.Taxonomy ENV_husbandry — Environment and: A documented purpose of controlling cross-border livestock herds, grazing rights or responsibility for straying animals. Disease prevention requires its own evidence and code.
historical_codebook.Correction release 23 October 2026: Six regional AI reviewers and root integration; same model contexts, not independent human or different-model verification. Source access and unresolved attributes remain explicit.
historical_codebook.Endpoint meanings: Chronology phases records observed reopening as Yes, No or Unknown. Scheduled expiry, legal transition and last observation are not observed reopening. Partial resumption applies only to the named traffic and direction.
historical_codebook.Duration arithmetic: Minimum and maximum values are date-boundary differences. Endpoint inclusion is recorded separately and does not trigger an automatic +1 day. Reported order lengths and clock times remain source-specific.
historical_codebook.Map continuity: Confirmed evidence stops at its dated limit. The following state is unknown unless the same scoped phase has an observed reopening. Unmarked geography never establishes openness.
historical_codebook.Held evidence visibility: A contested phase supplies held date markers at its recorded boundaries or observations, not a confirmed interval. The Atlas labels these markers and warns when a searched record has no evidence in the selected month. Two included records lack dated phases and remain searchable in All dates.
historical_codebook.Rwanda audit selection failure: GL01 had supported parent occurrence but freight-only child phases. The prior follow-up selection missed its passenger scope gap. Six scoped passenger observations/endpoints are now added; this finding does not establish completeness of other parent scopes.
historical_codebook.Correction dispositions: Follow-up review contains every previously unresolved record and every coverage finding. Audit changes records applied edits; the common export retains structured attribute and finding dispositions.
historical_codebook.Land and airport scope: Land-border register retained. Island-state air admission restrictions remain outside this release pending the separate airport integration. Short land closures are retained.
historical_codebook.Health and biosecurity / Food safety and: Preventing human exposure to unsafe or contaminated food, including aflatoxin or mycotoxin contamination, when explicitly attributed to the restricting authority or reported as its stated reason. Do not infer disease transmission, animal or plant pathogens, or protectionist intent from a food-safety restriction.

research_method.full_text: The dataset was compiled using OpenAI’s GPT‑6 Astra with Ultra reasoning, with GPT‑6 Astra Pro documented in the final research and review logs. The work comprised 16 initial research rounds, including three full-register verification exercises, followed by two further register-wide reviews and 50 additional research and review cycles. Six regional AI reviewers contributed to major assessments, with research, challenge and adjudication conducted in separate contexts of the same model. Reviewers checked whether each restriction occurred, its start and endpoint, the crossings and types of movement affected, continuity, and the reported reasons against linked source evidence. The two subsequent register-wide exercises comprised a blind reconstruction and challenge of 653 records, producing 3,918 claim assessments, and a further assessment of all 686 records and 738 phases in the expanded register. Additional chronology work assessed 519 cases and subjected 272 unresolved cases to fresh research and separate review. The final 50 cycles comprised 30 coverage-search cycles, ten targeted-verification cycles and ten audits of preselected records, providing full-record source reviews of 160 entries and addressing 176 targeted questions across 162 entries. Proposed additions were checked against existing episodes to avoid duplication, while partial reopenings and changes in restrictions were recorded as separate phases. The resulting register contains 829 records and 1,010 phases, supported by a catalogue of 4,680 distinct recorded URLs. Automated consistency checks covered the complete final dataset; uncertain dates, source-access limitations and unresolved claims remain explicit. The five register-wide reviews covered successive versions of the dataset, while the later targeted audits examined selected records.

duration_review.precision_rule: Retain supported date bounds and endpoint meanings. Observed same-cohort reopening, legal change, announced expiry and last-confirmed observation are distinct. Partial resumption applies only to its stated traffic and direction.
duration_review.counting_rule: Minimum and maximum durations are calendar-date boundary differences, not measured elapsed hours. Endpoint inclusion is recorded separately and never adds an automatic day. Same-day and intermittent regimes have no continuous whole-day duration.
duration_review.mapping_rule: Each included phase has its own reviewed geographical-scope decision. Sourced crossing-area coordinates are attached only to explicitly applicable phases. Unlocated or rejected matches acquire no inferred point or whole-frontier fallback. Wider lines and country outlines are reference context, not closure footprints; incomplete coverage remains explicit.
duration_review.coverage_rule: This is an incomplete, nonrandom inventory. Search and evidence coverage do not measure closure incidence, prove absence, or support causal comparisons. Overlapping parents, phases and rationale groups are not independent counts.
duration_review.rationale_rule: Rationale assignments are attributed and nonexclusive. Preserve official explanations, protest demands and analytical coding with their evidence and qualifications; a documented reason does not establish every motive.
duration_review.verification_rule: Research, source challenge and adjudication used separate contexts of the same AI model. Source access and unresolved claims remain explicit; independent human verification of every entry is not implied.
duration_review.continuity_rule: Temporal display follows each current phase and its explicit rule. Evidence does not extend beyond its dated limit; a last observation is not reopening or proof of later continued closure.
duration_review.held_rule: Held or contested phases remain discoverable at their recorded evidence dates. They are excluded from numeric continuous-duration claims, confirmed interval animation and supported phase-start filtering.
duration_review.scope_rule: The core register covers land-frontier restrictions, including international river-crossing services. Selected Australia, New Zealand and United Kingdom passenger-policy histories remain a separate country-context supplement and do not enter land-border counts or duration charts.

codebook.Interstate disputes and pressure: Political confrontation, retaliation, sanctions or pressure between states or territorial authorities across a frontier. Includes regional sanctions and disputes over territorial status or border administration. De facto authorities are identified without deciding sovereignty. Exclusions: Do not add merely because a closure crosses a border, follows fighting, or involves a foreign actor. A political dispute or pressure mechanism must be documented.
codebook.Power and regime politics: Seizure, retention or contestation of governing power, regime legitimacy or control of public institutions. Includes coups, succession, political opposition, democratic reform and conflict between rival governing or party authorities, including transnational party conflicts. Exclusions: Routine policy or livelihood demands alone do not establish regime contestation. External sanctions seeking a regime change belong under Interstate disputes and pressure unless a separate domestic mechanism is also evidenced.
codebook.Policy and socioeconomic demands: Documented demands to change public policy, employment, services or economic conditions, where the obstruction is intended to press those demands. Code the demand, not merely the fact that a protest occurred. Exclusions: Do not infer specific demands from an unspecified protest or use this label for every strike. Regime change or institutional power contests belong under Power and regime politics.
codebook.Health and biosecurity: Health and biosecurity replaces Public health. Human disease control and animal/plant disease control remain distinct. Health-policy opposition belongs under Policy and socioeconomic demands.
codebook.Security / Armed conflict and military c: Hostilities, armed-group control, military standoffs or threatened military action. Does not settle responsibility or establish a hidden military objective.
codebook.Security / Armed attacks and terrorism: A reported attack, assassination or threat of armed attack. Terrorism allegations remain attributed; inclusion does not itself designate an actor as terrorist.
codebook.Security / Crime and law enforcement: Crime prevention, criminal investigations, kidnappings or law-enforcement concerns beyond the separately coded smuggling purpose.
codebook.Security / Smuggling and illicit traffic: Preventing or responding to alleged illicit movement of goods, currency, weapons or people. Allegations are not treated as established criminal findings.
codebook.Security / Public order and immediate sa: Protection of travellers, staff or property; crowd control, unrest, safe port operation or event security.
codebook.Security / Espionage and hostile interfe: Attributed intelligence threats, espionage or deliberate cross-border interference. Allegations, including instrumentalised migration, remain attributed rather than established.
codebook.Security / Unspecified security: Security is supported at the broad level, but a more specific purpose is not established.
codebook.Health and biosecurity / Human disease c: Preventing introduction or transmission of human disease, including screening, quarantine and disinfection. Opposition to health rules is coded under policy demands.
codebook.Health and biosecurity / Animal and plan: Veterinary, phytosanitary and other animal/plant biosecurity objectives. Does not imply a human-health threat or a protectionist intention.
codebook.Trade and protectionism / Import, export: Restrictions on goods or market access, including economic protection and documented export controls. An instrument can establish the restriction without establishing all underlying motives.
codebook.Trade and protectionism / Customs and tr: Customs, tariffs, routing, vehicle eligibility or cargo-transfer rules that are themselves the documented rationale or policy content.
codebook.Trade and protectionism / Currency contr: Restrictions associated with banknote withdrawal, currency circulation or financial controls.
codebook.Trade and protectionism / Trade and tran: Commercial actors obstructing passage to seek changes in trade rules, market access, transport charges or customs services. Does not imply a government protectionist closure.
codebook.Trade and protectionism / Unspecified tr: A commercial or trade-policy rationale is recorded, but the evidence does not support a narrower subtype.
codebook.Migration / Entry and asylum control: Regulating or preventing migration admission, including nationality and asylum procedures. A travel restriction solely for health or security is not automatically a migration rationale.
codebook.Migration / Exit control: A documented migration purpose concerning departure. Direction alone does not establish this rationale.
codebook.Migration / Transit control: A documented migration purpose concerning onward passage. Direction alone does not establish this rationale.
codebook.Migration / Processing capacity: Suspension to reassign personnel or facilities to processing migrant arrivals.
codebook.Migration / Admission and document dispu: Disputes or protests over admission, repatriation, transit permission or travel documents. This includes demands to allow passage, not only efforts to prevent it.
codebook.Migration / Unspecified migration ration: Migration is recorded as relevant, but purpose or direction remains insufficiently resolved.
codebook.Electoral politics / Election administra: Conduct, integrity, staffing or security of voting. Add Security only where a security/public-order justification is separately recorded.
codebook.Electoral politics / Electoral disputes: Restrictions or obstruction connected to an explicitly documented dispute over an election, its result or a transition timetable.
codebook.Electoral politics / Voter access and pa: Obstruction intended to affect travel by voters or participation in an election.
codebook.Interstate disputes and pressure / Sanct: Border restrictions used to obtain concessions or change another authority's conduct, including formal regional sanctions. Includes clearly attributed reporting interpretations.
codebook.Interstate disputes and pressure / Diplo: Restrictions connected to a documented dispute, retaliatory measure or rupture of relations between authorities.
codebook.Interstate disputes and pressure / Terri: Disputes over boundaries, cross-border works, territory or sovereign status. Coding does not determine sovereignty or recognise de facto authorities as states.
codebook.Interstate disputes and pressure / Unspe: An interstate or inter-authority dispute is recorded without sufficient detail for a narrower subtype.
codebook.Power and regime politics / Coups and su: Seizure, transfer or consolidation of governing power, including a documented coup or succession context. Does not infer a distinct closure motive absent evidence.
codebook.Power and regime politics / Opposition a: Contestation of leadership, regime legitimacy, political participation or constitutional reform.
codebook.Power and regime politics / Contested go: Rival institutions, parties or armed authorities contesting jurisdiction or control of a crossing.
codebook.Power and regime politics / Unspecified: A power or regime dispute is recorded, but a narrower purpose is not established.
codebook.Policy and socioeconomic demands / Oppos: Demands to remove or change pandemic restrictions, testing rules or health-policy charges. Does not imply infection prevention as the protest's purpose.
codebook.Policy and socioeconomic demands / Jobs,: Employment, wages, working conditions, public services, infrastructure or household economic demands.
codebook.Policy and socioeconomic demands / Right: Documented grievances concerning rights, policing, land, environmental projects or a specified policy dispute outside the other subtypes.
codebook.Policy and socioeconomic demands / Unspe: A policy or socioeconomic purpose is established but cannot be narrowed. Do not use merely because unspecified protesters oppose a government.

locations.Marker precision: common road-crossing area reference; vehicle and pedestrian lanes distinct

UNHCR November 11 operational release confirms actual refugee reception at Hamdayet during the preceding days; this is not proof of general repeal. Scope remains Kassala and ordinary operational duration remains unknown.
audit_changes.Reason / adjudication: The UNHCR operational release directly confirms refugee reception at Hamdayet by November 11. Add the actual humanitarian exception while leaving the ordinary Kassala policy endpoint unresolved.

audit_changes.Before: Evidence is specific to Shushme trade; do not extend chronology to all Iran–Iraq posts or passengers.
audit_changes.After: May 3 truck passage is directly documented, but a full April 28 Iranian customs statement claims earlier reopening. Evidence is specific to Shushme freight.
audit_changes.Reason / adjudication: The full April 28 customs account reports an earlier Shushmi opening, while the Reuters May 3 shot list and interview directly establish movement on that later date. Hold the continuous duration until the difference in operational scope is explained; retain both dated claims.

audit_changes.After: Erez business passage occurred October 8–10 during the extended holiday restriction, then resumed October 15 after another interruption. audit_changes.Reason / adjudication: PCHR’s first weekly table and explicit partial-opening note establish business passage October 8–10, interrupting the earlier asserted continuous spell. Split the business-category restriction at that opening and the subsequent October 11 interruption; retain the category scope and ordinary non-operating-day caveat.

A January 2023 state article prints 2022 and a December 1, 2021 article prints September 26; contemporary November 25 closed-since-July reporting, actual November 27 cargo and later operational chronology favour November 2021. Pangsai remained closed in January 2022 and has no shared endpoint.
audit_changes.Reason / adjudication: Contemporary November 25 planning, actual November 27 cargo and the later operational account support November 26, 2021. The December article internally prints both September and November; disclose that conflict and the separate year error, with no Pangsai endpoint inferred.

audit_changes.Reason / adjudication: The full May 5 ministerial report establishes admission processing for 280 waiting trucks under health controls. Add the documented exception, without inferring driver nationality or treating June freight restoration as the first permitted movement.

audit_changes.Before: June 4 confirms international freight reopening, not passenger reopening. Differing accounts of contact-free trade ending concern a different operational measure. The combined regime does not support an all-traffic continuous interval.
audit_changes.After: June 4 concerns international freight restoration, not passenger reopening or the first permitted truck entry. May 5 waiting-truck admission, rail substitution and screened returns preclude an all-traffic continuous interval. Differing dates for the end of contact-free trade concern another operational measure.
audit_changes.Reason / adjudication: The full May 5 ministerial report establishes admission processing for 280 waiting trucks under health controls. Add the documented exception, without inferring driver nationality or treating June freight restoration as the first permitted movement.

audit_changes.Before: Start is official legal date. No common actual land reopening established; airport reopening must not be substituted.
audit_changes.After: Cameroon-side Ngueli reopening June 20 2021 verified separately from Chad June 17 ceremony. National common land reopening remains unknown.
audit_changes.Reason / adjudication: June 18 field reporting directly observes Cameroon refusing ordinary travellers after Chad’s opening, and the June 20 report identifies Cameroon’s separate official restoration. Add a crossing-specific formal phase rather than invent a national reopening date.
